title: Cut the 0.3.0 release (lockstep version bump, full changelog reconstruction, notices)
acceptance_criteria: All four @livecore packages and the workspace root are bumped in lockstep from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0: each packages/*/package.json version, each packages/*/src/index.ts VERSION constant and the root package.json. 0.3.0 is a MINOR bump per docs/23 because everything merged since v0.2.0 is additive (new routes, new contract fields, new SDK resource methods, new design tokens; nothing removed or narrowed). A dated entry ## [0.3.0] - <today> is added to the root CHANGELOG.md and to each affected package CHANGELOG (contracts, sdk-ts, design-tokens; ui-core gets a lockstep entry stating no package-level change). The changelog is reconstructed from the FULL commit range git log v0.2.0..HEAD, NOT just the existing Unreleased block: only CORE-SDX-001 left an Unreleased note, so the other ~14 changes (CORE-APROJ-001 through 004, CORE-PSELF-001, CORE-INV-001/002, CORE-ALC-001/002, CORE-VSEAL-001/002, CORE-PUSH-001/002, CORE-DTOK-001) must each be captured under the correct Added/Changed heading in the right package. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and the four per-package copies are regenerated with scripts/generate-third-party-notices.ps1 -Write, and the README package badge tracks 0.3.0. No git tag is pushed - pushing v0.3.0 stays the operator final manual step.
required_tests: The full local CI-equivalent is green at 0.3.0: dotnet build/test LiveCore.slnx, dotnet format verify, pnpm lint and format:check, pnpm --recursive build and test, the version-lockstep test (pnpm run test:versions), the per-package build and pack tests (they fail if VERSION, package.json and the changelog top entry disagree), the THIRD-PARTY notice drift gate in check mode, the publish dry-run gate logic (scripts/test-release-version.ps1 and scripts/test-package-publish.ps1) at 0.3.0, and scripts/boundary-scan.ps1. No new product test is required; keep the existing gates green and confirm the lockstep test seeded drift still differs at 0.3.0.
notes: Mirrors CORE-REL-001 (the 0.2.0 cut, commit c4ea34e) - read it and docs/23_PACKAGE_VERSIONING.md How to cut a release first. Pure release-cut: no route, table, event, migration, dependency or published API surface change - only versions, changelogs, notices and the README badge. Do NOT edit the backlog CSVs. Commit subject exactly CORE-REL-003: cut the 0.3.0 release .... Under the new branch-protection policy this lands via a feature branch and a reviewed PR, never a direct push to main.

title: Add a changelog-completeness gate so a package-surface change cannot ship undocumented
acceptance_criteria: A CI-runnable gate fails when a change to a published package typed surface (packages/contracts/src, packages/sdk-ts/src, packages/design-tokens/src, packages/ui-core/src) has landed since the last release tag without a non-empty ## [Unreleased] section in that package CHANGELOG.md and the root CHANGELOG.md. The gate follows the existing drift-gate pattern: a PowerShell module/script under scripts/ plus a pnpm script wired into the typescript CI job. It checks presence of Unreleased content for changed packages, not entry-to-commit matching, so it is robust and low-noise. Motivated by the 0.3.0 cut where 14 of 15 stories changed the package surface but left no changelog entry.
required_tests: A gate-logic test in the scripts/test-*.ps1 style proves the check passes when an Unreleased entry exists for a changed package and fails closed when a package src change since the last tag has an empty Unreleased section; it runs green on the tree once CORE-REL-003 has cut 0.3.0; the boundary scan stays green.
notes: Additive tooling and test only; no product or API surface change; product-neutral per docs/04. This is the root-cause fix for the changelog gap found while cutting 0.3.0. Independent of CORE-REL-003 but recommended before the next release. Lands via a feature branch and a reviewed PR.
